text:
**Philip Rubin** is a distinguished scientist and leader whose work spans speech science, cognitive psychology, and science policy. He earned a BA in psychology and linguistics from Brandeis University (1971) and a PhD in experimental psychology from the University of Connecticut (1975). Rubin is renowned for pioneering articulatory synthesis modeling of speech production, notably developing the ASY and SWS synthesis programs in the 1970s. His research advances include computational models of speech gestures, sinewave speech perception, signal processing (HADES), and multimodal audiovisual speech integration. His theoretical contributions emphasize dynamical systems approaches to speech, embodied cognition, and perceptual organization.
In science policy, Rubin held leadership roles such as Director of the Division of Behavioral and Cognitive Sciences at the NSF (2000-2003) and Assistant Director for Social, Behavioral, and Economic Sciences at the White House OSTP. He chaired key committees on research ethics, human subjects protection, and advocated for modernization of policies. Rubin has been President and Chair of the Federation of Associations in Behavioral and Brain Sciences (FABBS) and served on multiple advisory and trustee boards, including Haskins Laboratories and the University of Connecticut. His expertise is recognized through numerous fellowships and awards from leading societies in acoustics, psychology, and science administration. Additionally, Rubin’s influence extends into popular culture through sinewave synthesis work inspiring sound design and artistic projects.
